en.title: Unhinged: Zoë Kravitz, Sadie Sink Star in Netflix's New Horror Game
en.summary: Netflix is doubling down on interactive entertainment with Unhinged, a new first-person horror game from Oxenfree developer Night School Studio. The game boasts a star-studded cast including Zoë Kravitz and Sadie Sink, promising a mature, blood-spattered narrative experience.
en.body:
Netflix is once again venturing into the realm of interactive storytelling with **Unhinged**, a brand-new horror game developed by the acclaimed **Night School Studio**, the minds behind the beloved narrative adventure **Oxenfree**. This upcoming title marks a significant step for Netflix Games, moving beyond simple interactive movies to deliver a full-fledged video game experience.

Unlike the more subdued, teen-focused narrative of **Oxenfree**, **Unhinged** promises a darker, more mature tone. The game plunges players into a first-person horror scenario centering on two young women in adjacent homes, as one desperately tries to survive a terrifying home invasion. Adding significant star power to the project are **Sadie Sink**, known for her roles in *Stranger Things* and *Spider-Man: Brand New Day*, and **Zoë Kravitz**, celebrated for her work in *The Batman* and *Divergent*. The cast is further bolstered by the inclusion of veteran voice actor **Troy Baker**. The game is designed to leverage the ubiquitous smartphone, allowing players to interact with the world through in-game calls and texts, and even control a virtual flashlight.

## A New Breed of Netflix Gaming

**Unhinged** is not a passive viewing experience; it’s a game you actively play, streamed directly to your television via the Netflix platform. This approach distinguishes it from Netflix's previous forays into interactive content, such as the *Black Mirror: Bandersnatch* experience. Night School Studio's game director, Sam Warner, drew inspiration from innovative gameplay mechanics found in titles on the Nintendo DS and Wii, aiming to create a novel and engaging play experience. "If you've got Netflix and you have a phone, then this is for you," Warner stated, highlighting the game's accessibility. The developers have confirmed that the narrative features multiple branching paths and that player choices can indeed lead to death, encouraging replayability.

## What Fans Can Expect

The anticipation for **Unhinged** is palpable among fans of narrative games and horror enthusiasts alike. The combination of **Night School Studio**'s proven track record in crafting compelling stories and the star power of **Kravitz** and **Sink** creates a potent draw. This project signals Netflix's commitment to expanding its gaming division with high-quality, accessible titles that leverage its existing subscriber base. Gamers are eager to see how the studio will translate its signature atmospheric storytelling into a first-person horror context, especially with such a high-profile cast.

## Looking Ahead

**Unhinged** is set to launch on June 30, 2026, and will be available to all Netflix subscribers at no additional cost. The game is designed to be experienced in a single sitting, with its runtime mirroring that of a typical Netflix series episode, lasting just under an hour, but its replayable nature is key to exploring its full narrative potential.

content_raw: Netflix is dipping its toe back into narrative adventure with the upcoming launch of Unhinged , a first-person horror game from Oxenfree developer Night School Studio. Unlike the teen drama of Oxenfree, Unhinged looks to be a more mature, blood-spattered affair. The game's story centers on two young women in neighbouring houses, as one attempts to escape a home invasion. Unhinged also features bonafide acting talent, in the shape of Stranger Things and Spider-Man: Brand New Day star Sadie Sink, plus The Batman and Divergent's Zoë Kravitz. Video game veteran Troy Baker rounds out the cast list, meanwhile. Rather than Netflix's previous experiments with interactive live-action experiences (such as in Black Mirror's Bandersnatch), this is very much a video game that you control with your phone, streamed to your TV via the Netflix platform. Gameplay makes use of your phone to receive phone calls and text messages, or to look around its world with a virtual flashlight. As you'd expect, the story features multiple avenues to explore — and yes, you can die. While the overall experience is timed to feel like an episode of a Netflix series — lasting just under an hour — it's designed to be replayable to explore different narrative branches. "We looked deeply at the Wii [and] the Nintendo DS," Night School game director Sam Warner told Rolling Stone . "I grew up with those, and I think that focus on novel innovative play was something that we really started this game with. If you've got Netflix and you have a phone, then this is for you." Unhinged launches on June 30, and will be available to all Netflix subscribers. Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor.
